long_biography.plain_text:
Childhood in Nazi-occupied Amersfoort left a lasting mark on Alfred Balm, whose family endured starvation before Canadian soldiers liberated their city. Decades later in Calgary, he supported surviving veterans and wrote publicly about the antisemitism he had witnessed during the occupation.

When Balm learned about a project commemorating murdered Jewish residents of Amersfoort, he and his wife Phyllis supplied most of its initial funding. The project places inscribed memorial stones near victims' former homes. His later study of art history also shaped a series of historical novels, including fiction about attempts to protect Dutch art during the Second World War.
